children: Argentina's mining exports jumped 75% year-on-year in the first half of 2026 to $4.74 billion, largely driven by lithium shipments, the Argentine Chamber of Mining Companies and the Rosario Board of Trade said in a report.
The value of mining shipments represents a first-half record, according to the joint report published late Monday.

• Lithium cemented its position as Argentina's second most important mining export, accounting for nearly a quarter of total shipments. That was fuelled by the launch of new operations and the expansion of others.
• Gold accounted for 61% of total mining shipments, the sector's top export, while silver ranked third. Both benefited from high international prices.
• Argentina, Chile and Bolivia form the so-called Lithium Triangle, with seven projects currently in operation and five under construction.
• Mining represented 10% of total Argentine exports in the first half of the year, the report added.
